content:
REASON FOR REFERRAL: Diagnostic test for congenital myopathy
Panel CM/CMD, Virtual panel = Core / Centronuclear myopathy

TEST
Test for sequence variants and exon deletions and duplications in a panel of genes that cause congenital myopathy by next generation sequencing1.
Sequence variants confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

RESULTS
Heterozygous DNM2 c.1856C>T p.(Ser619Leu) sequence variant detected
No exonic deletions or duplications detected2.

SUMMARY
The DNM2 c.1856C>T p.(Ser619Leu) sequence variant has been previously reported in the literature in association with centronuclear myopathy and has been shown to affect the function of the DNM2 protein4. It is therefore predicted to be pathogenic. 
This result is confirms the clinical diagnosis of a congenital myopathy.

FURTHER WORK
If possible, this patient?s parents should be tested to confirm the inheritance pattern in this family.

Reported by:    		Jo McCauley
Data checked by:	KP
Report authorised by:     Rachael Mein, 29 August 2019    


Notes
1The coding exons and splice sites (including upto +/-10bp flanking sequence) of genes involved in congenital myopathy have been screened by Illumina sequencing, following target capture by in-solution hybridisation. In-house validation has shown this method to have equivalent sensitivity to fluorescent Sanger sequencing, which detects >99% of point mutations. Please note that this technique has only been validated to detect small insertions and deletions up to 10 base pairs in length.
Variants in the triplicated/homologous repeat regions of NEB and TTN may not be detected due to sequence homology.? 
Sequence variants filtered using Ingenuity Variant Analysis? software.  Variants with general population frequency of >1% (according to ExAc data http://exac.broadinstitute.org) or are unlikely to be pathogenic have not been reported. 
2 Copy Number Variant (CNV) analysis was performed by read depth comparison of the coding regions of the captured genes.  A small number of exons have fallen outside the normal range but are unlikely to be significant so these regions have not been investigated further. CNV analysis was not possible for SEPN1 ex1 as this exon is not fully captured therefore point mutations in this exon are screened by Sanger sequencing.  
3 Assessment of pathogenicity is carried out using bioinformatics software Alamut.
4 Gibbs et al., Disease Model and Mechanisms (2014) 7; 157-161
